statement: Sample efficiency dominates time-to-75%. An airbench-style whitened CNN (frozen patch-whitening, dirac init, BN, label smoothing 0.1, translate 2, alternating flip, Lookahead), with Muon on the block convs, 50% of steps at 24 px, block widths 128/256/704 and batch 2048, reaches 0.7551 in 8.75 epochs at 5.43 s (E031). That is far ahead of the best public CIFAR-100 result (8.11 s) and the organizers' ResNet9 (59 s). E031 is a single run with a +0.21 pp margin and has not been replicated. The SGD-era lever rates do not transfer to the Muon line (resize ~0.4 pp/s, epochs ~0.75 pp/s, block-3 width ~0.6 pp/s). Under Muon, cutting epochs costs ~0.56 pp per second saved (E031: 0.23 pp for 0.41 s). Resize near 50% has no usable measurement yet (E034: 0.75 +/- 1.2 pp/s). Resize at 75% costs ~1.8 pp/s (E029). Levers can only be ranked once the noise floor is measured.

The accuracy-vs-epochs slope is not a fixed property of the regime. It depends on the optimizer, architecture and recipe, and it flattens near the recipe's ceiling. Measured slopes: 0.87 pp/ep (E002, SGD, heavy regularization), 0.27-0.52 pp/ep (later SGD recipes), 0.29-0.31 pp/ep under Muon between 8.75 and 11 ep (E027, E031). The slope must be measured per recipe over spans of >= 2 epochs or with replicated endpoints. Interpolating it from another recipe is unreliable (E009, E034's misread rate).

Reproduction: airbench96 128/384/576, 8.5 epochs, batch 1024, no TTA, compile+warmup in build gives a 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 and time <= 9.0 s on this A100-SXM4. Repeating the identical run twice gives a 3-seed-mean accuracy spread <= 0.3 pp and a time spread <= 0.2 s, which sets the noise floor for later verdicts.

Epoch sweep on the H1a1 recipe at 7, 8.5 and 10 epochs: accuracy rises monotonically by 0.4-1.0 pp per epoch and crosses 0.753 between 8 and 9.5 epochs. Time scales close to linearly with epochs, with an intercept <= 1.0 s.

Accuracy per FLOP is block-specific. Block-2 width (the largest FLOP share, 16x16) is cheap to cut (E012: 384->256 cost ~0.2 pp with +1 ep). Block-1 width binds (E019: 128->96 lost 0.52 pp but saved only 0.74 s, so block-1 time is not proportional to its FLOPs, probably because it is bandwidth-bound at 32x32). The claim that block-3 width binds rests only on E021 (+0.33 pp for 576->704, about 1 sd of a difference). That result may also be confounded with translate 4->2: the descriptions disagree on E013's translate. All of this was measured under SGD, and none of it has been re-checked on the Muon tip.
A 96/256/384 (or 128/256/384) airbench96-layout net, at whatever epoch count gives 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753, finishes at least 10% faster than the best feasible 128/384/576 configuration.
Frozen patch-whitening and dirac init are the main sample-efficiency components on CIFAR-100, as they are on CIFAR-10. Removing them raises epochs-to-75% substantially.
At a fixed epoch count near the feasibility edge, replacing frozen whitening init with a standard learned first conv lowers 3-seed accuracy by >= 1.0 pp, which is well outside noise.

Per-step work that does not scale with resolution is a growing share of time on the Muon tip. E031 averages ~25 ms per step over ~210 steps at batch 2048. Of that, ~1.66 ms is Muon (~0.95 ms Newton-Schulz bmm plus ~0.7 ms of small elementwise kernels, E026). Lookahead, BN and elementwise kernels, augmentation, interpolate and host gaps between graph replays add more. Removing this work (fewer or cheaper Newton-Schulz iterations, a whole-run graph) cuts time directly at equal math.

With only 4 pinned CPU cores, any CPU-side data pipeline (DataLoader, CPU augmentation) bottlenecks training. Holding the whole uint8 dataset on the GPU and doing flip, translate and cutout on the GPU removes that bottleneck.

Baseline: the unmodified submission_template recipe runs feasibly at roughly 50-70 s. Swapping only its data pipeline for a GPU-resident one with GPU augmentation cuts time by >= 20% with accuracy within +/-0.3 pp.

At batch ~1024 and ~400 steps per run, kernel-launch and Python overhead is significant. torch.compile(mode='max-autotune') or CUDA-graph capture in the untimed build reduces s/step. Eval must use a separate dynamic or padded path that stays legal for any B in 1..1024.

On the feasible airbench96 recipe, switching from default compile to max-autotune plus CUDA-graph capture of the train step cuts mean time by >= 8% with |delta accuracy| < 0.3 pp. Eval for B in {1, 7, 1024} completes in < 5 s.

Timed prepare work (GPU transfer, normalization, whitening PCA over all patches) is a non-negligible fixed cost. Computing whitening on a patch subset and fusing preprocessing shrinks it at no accuracy cost.
Computing the whitening eigendecomposition on <= 5,000 images instead of the full set cuts mean time by >= 0.15 s, with accuracy change within noise (|delta| < 0.3 pp).

Low-resolution steps are cheaper but less useful, and their cost depends on the optimizer and is nonlinear in the low-res fraction. Under SGD, 33-50% at 24 px cost ~0.4 pp per second saved (E008, E013, E018). Under Muon, 75% at 24 px cost ~1.8 pp/s (E029), which points to a threshold once the 32 px phase gets short. Near 50% under Muon the cost is unmeasured within noise (E034). Data filtering is dead (E016).

Proxy-based data filtering: a tiny proxy net scores each batch, and the main net trains only on the highest-loss half. This saves more backward compute than the proxy pass and the extra epochs cost, as airbench96_faster does on CIFAR-10.

airbench96_faster-style filtering (proxy 32/64/64, keep the top 50% by loss) on the best feasible recipe reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time at least 10% lower than the best unfiltered feasible run.

Progressive resizing: a 24 px step costs ~0.68x a 32 px step under per-step graphs (E008). Under SGD, 33-50% schedules lost ~0.4 pp per second saved, independent of antialias (E008, E013, E018). The cost is nonlinear above ~50%: E029 (75% at 24 px under Muon) lost 1.36 pp, which suggests the run needs >= ~4-5 epochs at the 32 px test resolution, while LR is still meaningful, for features and BN statistics to adapt. Whether resize near 50% beats cutting epochs under Muon is unresolved (E034 +0.18 pp for +0.24 s is within noise).

Training the first ~50% of epochs at 24 px and the rest at 32 px cuts time by >= 10% compared with a 32 px run of equal epoch count, with accuracy loss <= 0.3 pp. Compiled graphs for both resolutions are built in build.

The airbench constants were tuned for long CIFAR-10 runs and are mis-tuned for a ~9-epoch 100-class run. Weakening regularization raised accuracy at fixed epochs under SGD (E004 +1.26 pp, E011 +0.35 pp), and the same holds under Muon (E030: translate 4 cost -0.62 pp). Muon on the block convs is the largest single optimizer lever found (+0.78 pp, E025/E026). Under SGD at >= 210 steps the run was sample-limited, and batch was a pure throughput lever (E015, E024, E028). Under Muon, step count binds below ~200 steps (E032). Schedule constants (whiten_bias_epochs 3, warmup, LR floor, Lookahead cadence) remain untested at this budget.

The best regularization strength scales with the epoch budget, under both SGD and Muon. At ~9-11 epochs the net under-fits, so weaker augmentation helps: cutout off (E004), translate 2 beats 4 (E011 +0.35 under SGD, E030 +0.62 under Muon). Label smoothing near 0.1 looks near-optimal (E014: LS 0 gave -0.31 pp, within noise). Translate 1 or 0 under Muon is untested.
At a fixed epoch count near the edge, removing cutout (or cutting it to 8 px) and lowering label smoothing to 0.1 raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.4 pp over the airbench96 defaults.

source: search:github.com/abdullah-athar/iterate-futurebiohackers/pull/3 ('Muon lost to SGD at every size')
statement: Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized momentum, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6) on the block conv filters beats tuned Nesterov SGD on this airbench-style net for CIFAR-100. At ~11 epochs it gives ~+0.8 pp at equal epochs (E025 +0.78, E026 +0.84), and spending that gain on epochs gave the fastest feasible runs (E027, E031). This contradicts the public CIFAR-100 report (futurebiohackers PR #3: 'Muon lost to SGD').
Replacing SGD with Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6) on the conv filters of the feasible airbench96 recipe at equal epochs raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp. Expected outcome: refuted.
Alternating (derandomized) horizontal flip gives a better gradient signal than random flip at short budgets, so it improves accuracy at fixed epochs on CIFAR-100 as it does on CIFAR-10.
Switching from random flip to alternating flip at a fixed epoch count near the edge raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at the same time cost.

source: results (E004, E007, E008, E009); review (Lvl1 coverage); search: lit C0037, C0039, C0040; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2 (airbench96 CIFAR-100 ceiling ~79%)
statement: Time-to-75% is set by the recipe's accuracy-per-step-cost curve. Optimizer geometry, averaging, regularization, resolution schedule and capacity together set both the per-epoch slope and the ceiling. Capacity value is block-specific (H1.2), but the evidence that block 3 / head features bind is weak and possibly confounded (E021). The cheapest feasible point keeps binding capacity, cuts low-value FLOPs and matches regularization to the epoch count.

source: results (E007, E009 post-mortem); search: lit C0039; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2
statement: Capacity ceiling: under the E004 recipe, 128/256/384 saturates near 75-75.5%, so extra epochs return only ~0.3 pp/epoch. The 128/384/576 net has a long-schedule ceiling around 79% and returns ~0.8-0.9 pp/epoch near 10 epochs. Because the narrow-net deficit follows a late-training width^-c law (C0039), it grows with epochs instead of shrinking.

On the E004 base, the accuracy gap between 128/256/384 and 128/384/576 is at least 0.5 pp larger at 12 epochs than at 8 epochs, with both widths run at both epoch counts. If the gap stays flat or shrinks, the ceiling mechanism is refuted and E009's flat slope came from noise or a recipe confound.

Noise floor on the Muon tip: rerunning E031 unchanged twice and E028 once, pooled with the originals, gives an sd of a 3-seed mean of about 0.15-0.25 pp and an sd of a run-to-run difference of about 0.25-0.35 pp, with same-seed nondeterminism dominating. If the pooled E031 mean falls below 0.7535, the tip reverts to E028 and E032-E035 are re-judged against the pooled baseline. From then on, any |delta| < 2 x sd(diff) is inconclusive.

Slope under the current recipe: cutting E004 from 10 to 9 epochs (schedule rescaled) lowers 3-seed accuracy by 0.5-1.0 pp and time by 0.8-1.0 s. In other words, the light-regularization wide net still gains >= 0.5 pp/epoch near 10 epochs.

source: search: lit C0038 (milder cut may still pay); results (E009)
statement: A milder width cut, 128/320/480 (same 3-conv layout, ~0.77x conv FLOPs/epoch), on the E004 recipe at about 11 epochs reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.4 s.

On the Muon tip E031 (128/256/704), using 2 convs per block instead of 3 (all else fixed, epochs raised so that time matches E031 within 0.1 s) gives 3-seed accuracy at least equal to E031's within the measured noise floor. In other words, depth per block is a cheaper lever than epochs.

source: results (E008); review (E008 follow-up top priority); search: lit C0024
statement: The E008 resize schedule (first 50% of steps at 24 px) on the E004 recipe, extended to 11 epochs (schedule rescaled), reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.3 s.

A 24/28/32 px curriculum by thirds of steps (bilinear downsample of the full augmented image, all shapes compiled and graphed in build) on the E004 recipe at 10.5-11 epochs reaches 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 at a mean time <= 8.2 s. It loses less accuracy per second saved than the 50%-at-24 px schedule.

On the Muon tip E031 (50% at 24 px), scaling translate to ~1 px during the 24 px phase only (2 px at 32 px) recovers >= 0.3 pp at equal time. Literature: lowering regularization at low resolution recovers resize loss (C0087/C0089).

source: review (H4.1.1 attribution); search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (LS 0.09)
statement: At 10 epochs on E004, lowering label smoothing from 0.1 to 0.05 (and separately to 0.0), changing nothing else, raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp for at least one of the two values.
At 10 epochs on E004, reducing translate from 4 px to 2 px (reflect padding), changing nothing else, raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time.

Regularization and budget interact. On a run of >= 12 effective epochs (e.g. a resize run extended for feasibility), adding cutout 8 back raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp, whereas at 10 epochs it lowers accuracy.

source: review (untried batch size); results (E007 post-mortem); search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (batch 1536)
statement: Under SGD with per-example LR held fixed and >= ~210 steps, the run is sample-limited, not step-limited: batch 768 to 2048 leaves accuracy within noise (E015, E024, E028) and larger batches buy throughput (-3.1%, -3.9%). This does not hold unconditionally under Muon. Batch 3072 (~140 steps) lost 1.04 pp (E032). That loss is confounded by the Lookahead sync count and warmup length (both tied to steps) and by ~1.7% of images dropped per epoch in the partial batch.
Batch 512 (lr scaled by the airbench convention) at 10 epochs on E004 raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.5 pp at a time cost <= +10%, which lets epochs be cut to below E004's time at accuracy >= 0.753.

source: search: raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench/master/legacy/airbench96.py; arxiv.org/html/2404.00498v2 (bias scaling 18->13.5 ep); lit C0011-C0013
statement: airbench schedule constants tuned for 37 epochs (or CIFAR-10 at 8 epochs) are off-optimal at ~9 epochs on CIFAR-100: warmup, LR end value, whiten_bias_epochs 3, momentum 0.85 and bias_scaler. The actual LR end value is disputed. The E035 post-mortem says the schedule ends at ~7% of peak, while H4/H4.5.1 assume decay to 0. The LR table in the tip commit must be read before any schedule test. Later CIFAR-10 records (hiverge, Fable) train the whitening bias for only 0.2 epochs.

source: search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (LR floor 0.05 with EMA tail)
statement: After reading the actual LR end value in the E031 commit, an LR floor sweep on E031 (end at 0 vs the current value vs 15% of peak, changing nothing else) shows a spread of >= 0.3 pp across the three settings. The best setting differs from the current one.

source: results (E008 16% vs ~22% FLOP saving); review (H2 profiling); search: raw.githubusercontent.com/fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun/main/investigations/24px-curriculum.md
statement: Per-step work that does not scale with resolution (eager SGD + Lookahead updates, BN/elementwise kernels, augmentation, interpolate) is a sizable share of the ~19 ms step. That is why a 24 px step costs ~0.68x rather than ~0.56x of a 32 px step (E008). Fusing the optimizer into compiled foreach ops inside the captured graph cuts it.

source: search: fulcrumresearch champion recipe (whole-run CUDA graph, fused foreach optimizer)
statement: Moving the SGD + Lookahead update into compiled torch._foreach_* ops inside the captured train-step graph (per-step LR from a precomputed GPU table) cuts E004's mean time by >= 4%, with |delta accuracy| < the measured noise floor.

source: results (E006 side observation: 0.146 s vs 0.062-0.066 s prepare)
statement: Warming the H2D transfer and allocation path in build on synthetic tensors of the real data shape removes the ~0.08 s first-trial prepare overhead. First-trial prepare then falls to <= 0.08 s, giving ~0.02-0.03 s off the 3-trial mean.

A torch.profiler run of E031 (a few hundred steps at each of 24 and 32 px) shows >= 2.0 ms per step of time that does not scale with resolution: the Muon Newton-Schulz and elementwise kernels, the SGD+Lookahead foreach updates, augmentation, interpolate, index gathers and host gaps. That is >= 10% of a 24 px step. The profile also records the actual Newton-Schulz iteration count (3 or 5).

On E031, capturing the whole training run (or each resolution phase) as one CUDA graph cuts mean time by >= 4%, with |delta accuracy| within the noise floor, and lowers the 24 px / 32 px step-cost ratio to <= 0.62. In this design, augmented batches are staged into per-step buffers by batched kernels inside the timed train (precomputing outside the timed region is illegal), and the LR, Lookahead and Muon scalars come from a GPU table.

source: review (H4/H4.4 bookkeeping); search: fable champion recipe (batch 1536); airbench94_muon (batch 2000)
statement: On E023, batch 1536 at equal epochs and equal per-example LR and wd (schedule tied to step count, graph recaptured in build) cuts mean time by >= 4% with |delta accuracy| <= 0.3 pp.

Block-3 dose-response on the Muon tip E031: widening block 3 from 704 to 896 (head input matched, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +0.35 s. That is a rate >= 0.85 pp/s, which beats the ~0.56 pp/s cost of cutting epochs under Muon.
Cutting block 2 from 256 to 192 on the Muon tip E031 (128/192/704, nothing else changed) saves >= 0.3 s and loses <= 0.2 pp, i.e. <= 0.6 pp/s, about the epoch-cut rate under Muon.

source: search: raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench/master/legacy/airbench96.py (3 convs with residual over the last two; widths 128/384/512)
statement: If the current net lacks the original airbench96 residual over the last two convs of each block (x = x + x0), adding it raises 3-seed accuracy on E031 by >= 0.3 pp at <= +2% time. Check the code first.

The 100-way linear head is limited by the dimension of the pooled feature vector, not by general block-3 capacity. Most of the gain from widening block 3 (E021) comes from the wider final representation, so a cheap expansion at the end of the net can buy it for fewer FLOPs than widening all three block-3 convs.
On the Muon tip, keeping block 3 at 576 and adding one 1x1 conv (576->1024, BN, GELU) before the final pooling reaches 3-seed accuracy >= E031's within noise at a lower mean time than E031.
On E031, concatenating global max and average pooling (doubling the head input, no conv change) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +1% time.

source: search: legacy/airbench96.py (whiten_bias_epochs 3); fable champion recipe (0.2-epoch whiten-bias phase)
statement: On E031, cutting whiten_bias_epochs from 3 to 0.2 (nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time. Training the whitening bias for ~1/3 of an 8.75-epoch run is a 37-epoch leftover, and the hiverge and Fable CIFAR-10 records both use 0.2 epochs.

source: review (larger low-res fraction untried); results (E013, E018, E021)
statement: On E023, with the margin bought by N4 (block 3 at 896), raising the 24 px fraction from 50% to 70% of steps keeps 3-seed accuracy >= 0.753 and brings mean time to <= 6.4 s. The resize cost stays on the ~0.4 pp/s line, i.e. it does not steepen at higher fractions.

Conditional on H2.4.4 (whole-run graph, 24 px step <= 0.62x), a 24/28/32 curriculum by thirds on the Muon tip, with >= 40% of steps at 32 px, loses <= 0.4 pp per second saved, below the ~0.56 pp/s Muon epoch-cut rate.

source: review (Lvl1 coverage: optimizer geometry and averaging); results (E025, E032, E035); search: arxiv.org/abs/2411.18704; arxiv.org/html/2507.01598v4
statement: Update geometry plus iterate averaging set sample efficiency on the Muon line. Muon's fixed-norm orthogonalized steps do not shrink near convergence, so (a) the iterate stays noisy to the end, which makes weight averaging (Lookahead, EMA tail) first-order (E035: removing Lookahead cost 0.81 pp), and (b) total movement scales with step count, so the number of steps (~200+) is a resource and batch increases past ~2048 lose accuracy (E032). The cheapest remaining margin should come from tuning averaging and Muon's own constants at zero per-step cost, and that margin can then be spent on epochs.

source: results (E035 post-mortem); search: fable champion recipe (EMA tail every 4 steps, decay 0.7, LR floor 0.05); arxiv.org/abs/2411.18704
statement: Iterate averaging acts as the annealing that the short, high-LR Muon schedule does not fully provide. Stronger or better-placed averaging (Lookahead cadence and alpha, or a Fable-style EMA tail at an LR floor) raises accuracy at near-zero step cost.

On E031, a two-point Lookahead sweep (sync every k/2 steps, and separately a final alpha closer to the slow weights; current values read from code) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp for at least one setting at <= +1% time.

On E031, adding a Fable-style EMA tail on top of Lookahead raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +1% time. The tail averages every 4 steps with decay 0.7, starts 8 steps before the decay ends, uses the EMA weights for eval and resets the EMA state in prepare.

source: results (E032, E033); review (E032 confounds); search: arxiv.org/html/2507.01598v4 (Muon critical batch size)
statement: Under Muon, the step count binds below ~200 steps, because each step moves the filters by a fixed orthogonalized amount and Lookahead syncs are counted in steps. E032's -1.04 pp at batch 3072 is partly an averaging effect (fewer Lookahead syncs, shorter warmup), not only fewer Muon steps.

source: review (separate averaging from step size in E032)
statement: On E031 at batch 3072, holding the Lookahead cadence and warmup fixed in examples rather than steps (and not dropping the partial batch) recovers >= 0.5 pp of E032's 1.04 pp loss. If it recovers < 0.2 pp, the loss is from Muon step count, and batch stays at 2048.

Muon's own constants (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, fixed quintic Newton-Schulz coefficients, no update-magnitude schedule) come from airbench94_muon on CIFAR-10 and are slightly off-optimal here. The lr optimum is at or below 0.24 (E033: 0.32 cost 0.33 pp, within noise). The hiverge record uses lr 0.205, momentum 0.655 and an update magnitude that shrinks from 0.50 to 0.08.

source: search: hiverge baseline (lr 0.205, momentum 0.655); Fable (0.2255); results (E033)
statement: On E031, Muon lr 0.20 with momentum 0.65 (hiverge values, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp.

On E031, Polar-Express per-iteration Newton-Schulz coefficients at the same iteration count, with the update RMS matched to the current quintic's, change 3-seed accuracy by < 0.3 pp (a pre-registered likely null). Without RMS matching, the coefficient change is confounded with a hidden Muon lr change (C0118).

source: results (E026 Muon cost breakdown); search: lit D009/D010 (C0097, C0104, C0115, C0116); arxiv.org/html/2512.04632 (Turbo-Muon ~1%)
statement: Muon's per-step cost (~1.66 ms/step, ~0.35 s per run on E031) can be cut at equal accuracy. Small conv filters tolerate looser orthogonalization (C0097, C0104), so fewer Newton-Schulz iterations, a cheaper polynomial, or fused elementwise kernels save time without losing accuracy per step.

source: search: lit D009 (C0104, C0105); review (cut NS iterations after profiling)
statement: On E031, cutting Newton-Schulz by one iteration (e.g. 3->2 with aggressive per-iteration coefficients, or 5->3 if the code runs 5) saves >= 0.08 s per run with |delta accuracy| within the noise floor.

Diffing commits b0eba3b, 6d40ead and 12fffd2 settles whether E013 and E021 differ in translate amplitude. Independently, on the Muon tip E031, block 3 at 704 beats block 3 at 576 (time-matched by epochs) by >= 0.3 pp, pooled over 2 runs per arm. If not, the claim that block 3 binds (H1.2, H5.2) is dropped and 576 becomes the cheaper tip.

source: results (E030: translate 4 vs 2 cost -0.62 pp under Muon); review (translate 1 under Muon)
statement: On E031, reducing translate from 2 px to 1 px (both resolution phases, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time, extending the E030 trend under Muon.

source: search: lit D008 (C0079 FixRes); review (E029 discriminating test); results (E029)
statement: E029's threshold comes from test-resolution mismatch, not from FLOPs removed. At 75% of steps at 24 px on E031, either (a) moving 32 px steps out of the low-LR tail (32 px for steps 40-65%, 24 px elsewhere) or (b) adding a short forward-only 32 px BN-statistics recalibration on training batches at the end of the timed train recovers >= 0.6 pp of E029's 1.36 pp loss.

source: review (E034 unit mix-up and noise); results (E031, E034)
statement: A head-to-head on E031 with replicated endpoints (2 runs each) compares two cuts. One is 50% vs 30% of steps at 24 px. The other is 8.75 vs 7.75 epochs. They give rates with errors under +/-0.3 pp/s, and resize near 50% costs >= the epoch-cut rate (~0.56 pp/s), so less resize plus fewer epochs is the faster frontier under Muon.
